title: NEET UG Class 12 Revised Syllabus (NTA Updated)

Physics.name: Electric Charges and Fields
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Electric charges: Conservation of charge, Quantization of charge (q = ±ne)
Coulomb's law in vector form, force between two point charges, forces between multiple charges (superposition principle)
Electric field: Electric field due to a point charge, electric field lines and their properties
Electric dipole: Electric field due to a dipole on axial and equatorial lines
Torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field (τ = p × E) and potential energy of dipole (U = -p·E)
Electric flux (Φ = ∮ E·dA), Gauss's law in electrostatics
Applications of Gauss's law: Field due to infinitely long straight charged wire (E = λ / 2πε0r)
Field due to uniformly charged infinite plane sheet (E = σ / 2ε0)
Field due to uniformly charged thin spherical shell (inside E = 0, outside E = q / 4πε0r²)
Physics.keyConcepts: E_axial = 2kp/r³, E_equatorial = kp/r³, Gauss Law: Φ_net = q_enclosed / ε0, Shell theorem: Field inside conductor is zero

Physics.name: Electrostatic Potential & Capacitance
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Electric potential, potential difference, electric potential due to a point charge (V = kq/r)
Potential due to an electric dipole (V = kp cos θ / r²) and system of charges
Equipotential surfaces and their properties, relation between electric field and potential (E = -dV/dr)
Electrical potential energy of a system of two point charges and of electric dipole in an electrostatic field
Conductors and insulators, electrostatic shielding, free charges and bound charges inside a conductor
Dielectrics and electric polarization, dielectric constant K
Capacitors and capacitance, capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air (C0 = ε0A/d) and with dielectric medium (C = K ε0A/d)
Combination of capacitors in series and parallel, energy stored in a capacitor (U = 0.5 CV² = Q² / 2C)
Energy density of electrostatic field (u = 0.5 ε0 E²), redistribution of charges and loss of energy on sharing
Physics.keyConcepts: C = K ε0 A / d, In series: 1/C_eq = ∑(1/Ci), In parallel: C_eq = ∑Ci, U = 0.5 C V², Common potential V = (C1V1 + C2V2)/(C1 + C2)

Physics.name: Current Electricity
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Electric current, flow of electric charges in a metallic conductor, drift velocity (v_d = eEτ/m)
Mobility (μ = v_d / E) and its relation with electric current (I = n e A v_d)
Ohm's law, electrical resistance, V-I characteristics (linear and non-linear)
Electrical resistivity and conductivity, temperature dependence of resistance (R_t = R_0 (1 + αΔt))
Internal resistance of a cell, terminal potential difference (V = E - Ir) and emf of a cell
Combination of cells in series and parallel (mixed grouping condition for max current)
Kirchhoff's rules: Junction rule (conservation of charge) and Loop rule (conservation of energy)
Wheatstone bridge: balanced condition (P/Q = R/S), Meter Bridge for resistance measurement
Physics.keyConcepts: I = n A e v_d, R = ρL/A, Kirchhoff laws, Balanced Wheatstone: R1/R2 = R3/R4, Battery discharging V = E - Ir, charging V = E + Ir

Physics.unitName: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
Physics.name: Moving Charges and Magnetism
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Concept of magnetic field, Oersted's experiment
Biot-Savart law and its vector form, magnetic field due to current-carrying circular loop (axial and center B = μ0 I / 2R)
Ampere's circuital law and its applications: infinitely long straight wire, long solenoid (B = μ0 n I)
Lorentz force on a moving charge in magnetic and electric fields (F = q(E + v × B))
Motion of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field (helical and circular paths, radius r = mv/qB, time period T = 2πm/qB)
Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field (F = I (L × B))
Force between two parallel current-carrying conductors, definition of one Ampere
Torque experienced by a current loop in uniform magnetic field (τ = M × B, where M = NIA)
Moving Coil Galvanometer (MCG): current sensitivity, voltage sensitivity, conversion into Ammeter (low shunt resistance in parallel) and Voltmeter (high resistance in series)
Physics.keyConcepts: F = q(v × B), r = mv/qB, Force between parallel wires = (μ0 I1 I2 L)/(2πd), Shunt resistance S = (I_g G)/(I - I_g), Voltmeter R_s = (V/I_g) - G

Physics.unitName: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
Physics.name: Magnetism and Matter
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid, magnetic field lines and Gauss's law for magnetism (∮ B·dA = 0)
Magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron (Bohr magneton μ_B = eh/4πm)
Magnetic properties of materials: Diamagnetic, Paramagnetic, and Ferromagnetic substances
Curie's law for paramagnets (χ ∝ 1/T), Curie temperature for ferromagnets
Magnetic permeability (μ), magnetic susceptibility (χ), relation μ_r = 1 + χ
Physics.keyConcepts: Gauss law: isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist, Diamagnetic χ < 0, Paramagnetic χ > 0, Ferromagnetic χ >> 1, Curie-Weiss law

Physics.name: Electromagnetic Induction
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday's experiments, magnetic flux (Φ = B·A)
Faraday's laws of induction: induced emf e = -dΦ/dt
Lenz's law and conservation of energy, polarity of induced emf
Motional electromotive force (e = Bvl), induced current and power dissipation
Eddy currents: production, damping, induction furnace, minimization by laminated cores
Self-inductance (L): self-induced back emf (e = -L di/dt), inductance of a long solenoid (L = μ0 n² A l)
Mutual inductance (M): mutual induced emf (e = -M di/dt), coupling coefficient (k = M / √(L1L2))
Energy stored in an inductor (U = 0.5 L I²)
Physics.keyConcepts: e = -dΦ/dt, Motional emf e = Bvl, L = μ0 n² A l, Stored energy U = 0.5 L I², Lenz's law enforces conservation of energy

Physics.name: Alternating Current
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Alternating current and voltage, sinusoidal waveforms, peak value, mean/average value (I_avg = 2I0/π = 0.637 I0)
Root Mean Square (RMS) value of AC (I_rms = I0 / √2 = 0.707 I0)
AC circuit with pure resistor (current in phase with voltage)
AC circuit with pure inductor (current lags voltage by π/2, inductive reactance X_L = ωL)
AC circuit with pure capacitor (current leads voltage by π/2, capacitive reactance X_C = 1/ωC)
Series LCR circuit: Phasor diagrams, impedance (Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²)), phase angle (tan φ = (X_L - X_C)/R)
Resonance in series LCR circuit: resonant frequency (f_r = 1 / (2π√(LC))), sharpness of resonance, Q-factor (Q = ω0 L / R)
Power in AC circuits: instantaneous power, real power (P_avg = V_rms I_rms cos φ), power factor (cos φ = R/Z), wattless current
AC generator and Transformer: principle, step-up vs step-down, transformation ratio (N_s/N_p = V_s/V_p = I_p/I_s), energy losses
Physics.keyConcepts: Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²), Resonant frequency ω0 = 1/√(LC), Power factor cos φ = R/Z, Wattless current = I_rms sin φ, Transformer ratio

Physics.name: Electromagnetic Waves
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Displacement current: Maxwell's modification of Ampere's law (Ampere-Maxwell law)
Electromagnetic waves: characteristics, transverse nature (E and B perpendicular to each other and propagation direction)
Speed of EM waves in vacuum (c = 1 / √(μ0 ε0) = E0 / B0 = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
Energy density of EM waves (u = 0.5 ε0 E² + B² / 2μ0)
Electromagnetic spectrum: Radio waves, Microwaves, Infrared, Visible light, Ultraviolet, X-rays, Gamma rays
Wavelength ranges, production methods, detection, and important applications of each band
Physics.keyConcepts: c = E0 / B0 = 1/√(μ0 ε0), Intensity I = u·c, Radiation pressure P = I/c (absorbing) or 2I/c (reflecting), Order of spectrum frequencies

Physics.name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors: Mirror formula (1/v + 1/u = 1/f), magnification (m = -v/u)
Refraction of light: Snell's law (n1 sin i = n2 sin r), absolute and relative refractive indices
Total Internal Reflection (TIR): Critical angle (sin C = 1/n), applications (optical fibres, mirage, prisms)
Refraction at spherical surfaces (n2/v - n1/u = (n2 - n1)/R)
Thin lens formula (1/v - 1/u = 1/f), Lens Maker's formula (1/f = (n - 1) (1/R1 - 1/R2))
Power of a lens (P = 1/f in metres, Dioptres), combination of thin lenses in contact (P = P1 + P2)
Refraction of light through a prism: angle of deviation, angle of minimum deviation (n = sin((A + δ_m)/2) / sin(A/2)), dispersion
Optical instruments: Simple microscope, Compound microscope (magnification m = (L/f_o) · (D/f_e)), Astronomical telescope (reflecting and refracting, m = f_o / f_e)
Physics.keyConcepts: Lens maker's formula, Mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, Lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, TIR sin C = 1/μ, Microscope magnification m = -(v_o/u_o)(1 + D/f_e)

Physics.name: Wave Optics
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Wavefront and Huygens' principle: construction of secondary wavelets, reflection and refraction of plane waves using wave theory
Coherent and incoherent sources of light, condition for sustained interference
Interference of light: Young's Double Slit Experiment (YDSE)
Expression for path difference, constructive interference (Δx = nλ) and destructive interference (Δx = (2n-1)λ/2)
Fringe width (β = λD / d), intensity distribution in YDSE (I = 4 I0 cos²(φ/2))
Diffraction of light: Diffraction due to a single slit, central maximum width (2λD / a), secondary maxima and minima
Physics.keyConcepts: YDSE fringe width β = λD/d, Intensity I_max = (√I1 + √I2)², Central diffraction maximum width = 2λD/a, Minima condition a sin θ = nλ

Physics.unitName: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
Physics.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Photoelectric effect: Hertz and Lenard's observations, experimental study of photoelectric effect
Threshold frequency (ν0), work function (Φ0 = hν0), stopping potential (eV0 = K_max)
Failure of classical wave theory to explain photoelectric emission
Einstein's photoelectric equation: K_max = hν - Φ0 = e V0
Particle nature of light: Photons, photon energy (E = hν = hc/λ), photon momentum (p = h/λ)
Matter waves: de Broglie hypothesis, de Broglie wavelength of particle (λ = h/p = h / √(2mE) = h / √(2mqV))
de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential V (λ = 1.227 / √V nm = 12.27 / √V Å)
Physics.keyConcepts: eV0 = hν - hν0, λ_electron = 12.27 / √V Å, Stopping potential depends on frequency, not intensity; Photocurrent ∝ light intensity

Physics.name: Atoms
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Alpha-particle scattering experiment (Geiger-Marsden), Rutherford's nuclear model of atom, distance of closest approach, impact parameter
Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom: postulates (quantization of angular momentum L = nh/2π)
Derivation of radius of nth orbit (r_n = 0.529 n²/Z Å), velocity of electron (v_n = c/137 · Z/n)
Energy of electron in nth orbit: Kinetic energy, Potential energy, Total energy (E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV)
Hydrogen spectrum: Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund spectral series; Rydberg formula (1/λ = R (1/n1² - 1/n2²))
de Broglie's explanation of Bohr's second postulate of quantization
Physics.keyConcepts: r_n ∝ n²/Z, E_n ∝ -Z²/n², K = -E, U = 2E, Shortest wavelength (series limit) when n2 = ∞, Lyman series in UV, Balmer in visible

Physics.name: Nuclei
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Composition and size of nucleus: atomic masses, isotopes, isobars, isotones
Nuclear radius formula (R = R0 A^(1/3), where R0 = 1.2 × 10^-15 m), nuclear density is independent of mass number A
Mass defect (Δm = [Z m_p + (A - Z) m_n] - M_nucleus), Einstein's mass-energy equivalence (E = Δm c²)
Binding Energy (BE) and Binding Energy per nucleon (BE/A) curve vs mass number
Nuclear forces: properties (strongest in nature, short range, charge-independent, non-central, saturated)
Nuclear fission (e.g. U-235 fission, Q-value calculation) and Nuclear fusion (stellar energy, proton-proton cycle)
Physics.keyConcepts: R = R0 A^(1/3), 1 amu = 931.5 MeV, Nuclear density is constant (~2.3 × 10^17 kg/m³), BE/A peaks at Fe-56 (8.75 MeV/nucleon)

Physics.name: Semiconductor Electronics
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Energy bands in solids: Valence band, conduction band, forbidden energy gap (E_g in metals, semiconductors, insulators)
Intrinsic semiconductors (pure Si and Ge, n_e = n_h = n_i)
Extrinsic semiconductors: Doping, n-type (pentavalent impurities like P, As; n_e >> n_h) and p-type (trivalent impurities like B, Al, In; n_h >> n_e), mass action law (n_e · n_h = n_i²)
p-n junction formation: Diffusion and drift currents, depletion layer, barrier potential
p-n junction diode: Forward bias (depletion layer narrows, threshold/knee voltage) and Reverse bias (breakdown)
Diode as a rectifier: Half-wave rectifier (efficiency 40.6%, ripple factor 1.21) and Full-wave rectifier (center-tapped/bridge, efficiency 81.2%, ripple factor 0.48)
Special purpose diodes: Light Emitting Diode (LED), Photodiode, Solar cell (V-I characteristics and working principles)
Physics.keyConcepts: n_e · n_h = n_i², Forward bias: p to +, n to - (low resistance); Reverse bias: p to -, n to + (high resistance); Full wave rectifier frequency = 2f_in

Physics.name: Practical Physics & Experimental Skills
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Vernier calipers and Screw gauge (least count, zero error, measurement of diameter)
Simple pendulum: dissipation of energy by plotting a graph between square of amplitude and time
Metre scale: mass of a given object by principle of moments
Young's modulus of elasticity of the material of a metallic wire
Surface tension of water by capillary rise and effect of detergents
Coefficient of Viscosity of a given viscous liquid by measuring terminal velocity of spherical body
Speed of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube
Resistance and figure of merit of a galvanometer by half-deflection method
Focal length of concave mirror and convex lens using u-v method
Characteristic curves of a p-n junction diode in forward and reverse bias
Physics.keyConcepts: Least count = 1 MSD - 1 VSD, Pitch / Total head scale divisions, Meter bridge balanced bridge condition, u-v graph is rectangular hyperbola

Chemistry.name: Solutions
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Types of solutions, expressions of concentration of solutions (Molarity, Molality, Mole fraction)
Solubility of gases in liquids: Henry's law (p = K_H · x) and its applications
Vapour pressure of liquid solutions, Raoult's law for volatile solutes (P_total = P_A° x_A + P_B° x_B)
Ideal and non-ideal solutions, positive deviations (ethanol + acetone) and negative deviations (chloroform + acetone), Azeotropes
Colligative properties: Relative lowering of vapour pressure ((P° - P)/P° = i · x_solute)
Elevation of boiling point (ΔT_b = i · K_b · m), Molal boiling point elevation constant
Depression of freezing point (ΔT_f = i · K_f · m), Cryoscopic constant
Osmotic pressure (π = i · CRT), reverse osmosis and water purification
Abnormal molar masses, Van't Hoff factor (i), degree of dissociation (α = (i - 1)/(n - 1)) and association (α = (1 - i)/(1 - 1/n))
Chemistry.keyConcepts: ΔT_b = i K_b m, ΔT_f = i K_f m, π = i CRT, Van't Hoff factor: i > 1 for dissociation (NaCl i=2, BaCl2 i=3), i < 1 for association (acetic acid dimerizes i=0.5)

Chemistry.name: Electrochemistry
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Redox reactions, Galvanic cells, Daniel cell, Electrode potential, Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)
Electrochemical series and its applications (predicting spontaneity, reducing power)
Nernst equation: E_cell = E°_cell - (0.0591 / n) log Q at 298 K
Relationship between Gibbs free energy and cell EMF: ΔG° = -n F E°_cell = -2.303 RT log K_c
Conductance in electrolytic solutions: Specific conductance / conductivity (κ), Molar conductivity (Λ_m = κ × 1000 / M)
Variation of conductivity and molar conductivity with concentration (Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation for strong electrolytes)
Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions and its applications (Λ°_m of weak electrolytes, degree of dissociation α = Λ_m / Λ°_m)
Electrolysis: Faraday's laws of electrolysis (w = Z I t, w1/E1 = w2/E2)
Commercial cells: Primary batteries (dry cell, mercury cell), Secondary batteries (Lead-acid accumulator, Ni-Cd cell), Fuel cells (H2-O2 fuel cell), Corrosion of metals
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Nernst equation E = E° - (0.0591/n) log Q, ΔG° = -nFE°, Kohlrausch law: Λ°_m(CH3COOH) = Λ°_m(CH3COONa) + Λ°_m(HCl) - Λ°_m(NaCl), 1 Faraday = 96500 C

Chemistry.name: Chemical Kinetics
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Rate of reaction (average and instantaneous rates), factors affecting rate of reaction (concentration, temperature, catalyst)
Rate law, rate constant (k), order of reaction (0, 1, 2, fractional) and molecularity (elementary vs complex reactions)
Zero order reactions: integrated rate law ([A] = [A]0 - kt), half-life (t_1/2 = [A]0 / 2k)
First order reactions: integrated rate law (k = (2.303/t) log([A]0/[A])), half-life (t_1/2 = 0.693 / k)
Pseudo-first order reactions (acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate, inversion of cane sugar)
Temperature dependence of reaction rate: Arrhenius equation (k = A e^(-E_a / RT), log(k2/k1) = (E_a / 2.303 R) (1/T1 - 1/T2))
Concept of activation energy (E_a), catalyst effect (lowers activation energy), Collision theory of chemical reactions
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Units of rate constant k = (mol/L)^(1-n) s^-1, First order t_1/2 = 0.693/k is independent of initial concentration, Arrhenius slope = -E_a / 2.303 R

Chemistry.name: d- and f-Block Elements
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Transition elements (d-block): General characteristics, electronic configuration (exceptions: Cr 3d⁵ 4s¹, Cu 3d¹⁰ 4s¹)
General trends in 3d series: Metallic character, atomic and ionic radii, ionization enthalpies, variable oxidation states
Standard electrode potentials (E° values for M²⁺/M and M³⁺/M²⁺), magnetic properties (spin-only formula μ = √(n(n+2)) BM)
Formation of coloured ions (d-d transitions), catalytic properties, formation of interstitial compounds and alloys
Preparation, properties, and oxidizing actions of Potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7) and Potassium permanganate (KMnO4) in acidic, basic, neutral media
Inner transition elements (f-block): Lanthanoids - electronic configuration, oxidation states (+3 dominant, Ce⁴⁺, Eu²⁺), Lanthanoid contraction and its consequences
Actinoids: Electronic configuration, oxidation states, comparison with lanthanoids
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Lanthanoid contraction causes Zr-Hf and Nb-Ta to have nearly identical atomic radii, Spin-only magnetic moment μ = √(n(n+2)) BM, KMnO4 n-factor: 5 (acidic), 1 (basic), 3 (neutral)

Chemistry.name: Coordination Compounds
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Werner's coordination theory: primary (ionizable) and secondary (non-ionizable / coordination number) valencies
Ligands: monodentate, bidentate, polydentate (EDTA⁴⁻), ambidentate ligands (NO2⁻/ONO⁻, SCN⁻/NCS⁻), chelate effect
IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear coordination compounds
Isomerism in coordination compounds: Structural (ionization, hydrate/solvate, linkage, coordination) and Stereoisomerism (geometrical: cis-trans, fac-mer; optical isomerism)
Valence Bond Theory (VBT): inner orbital complexes (d²sp³, low spin) vs outer orbital complexes (sp³d², high spin), magnetic behaviour
Crystal Field Theory (CFT): Crystal field splitting in octahedral (t2g and eg) and tetrahedral complexes (Δ_t = 4/9 Δ_o)
Spectrochemical series, weak field vs strong field ligands, pairing energy (P vs Δ_o), colour of complexes
Importance and applications of coordination compounds (Cisplatin in cancer, Chlorophyll (Mg), Haemoglobin (Fe), Vitamin B12 (Co))
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Spectrochemical series: I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H2O < NH3 < en < CN⁻ < CO, Δ_o > P: pairing occurs (low spin), d²sp³ octahedral inner vs sp³d² outer

Chemistry.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Nomenclature, classification (1°, 2°, 3°, allylic, benzylic, vinylic, aryl halides), nature of C-X bond
Methods of preparation of haloalkanes: from alcohols (SOCl2 Darzens process, PCl5, PCl3, HX), from alkanes, and from alkenes
Halogen exchange reactions: Finkelstein reaction (R-Cl/Br + NaI → R-I) and Swarts reaction (R-Cl + AgF → R-F)

Nucleophilic substitution reactions: S_N1 mechanism (two steps, carbocation intermediate, racemization, 3° > 2° > 1°) and S_N2 mechanism (one step, bimolecular, transition state, Walden inversion, 1° > 2° > 3°)
Elimination reactions: Saytzeff (Zaitsev) rule, dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH
Reaction with metals: Grignard reagent (R-Mg-X) preparation, Wurtz reaction
Haloarenes: low reactivity of aryl halides towards nucleophilic substitution (resonance, sp² carbon, partial double bond character)
Electrophilic substitution in haloarenes (o,p-directing with halogen deactivation)
Wurtz-Fittig and Fittig reactions, environmental effects of polyhalogen compounds (Chloroform, Iodoform, Freons, DDT)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: S_N2: Walden inversion, rate = k[R-X][Nu⁻], favored in polar aprotic solvents (DMSO, DMF); S_N1: carbocation rearrangement, racemization; Zaitsev: more substituted alkene is major

Chemistry.name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Alcohols: Nomenclature, classification (1°, 2°, 3°), preparation from alkenes (acid hydration, hydroboration-oxidation: anti-Markovnikov), carbonyl compounds reduction, and Grignard reagents
Physical properties: Boiling points (intermolecular H-bonding), solubility in water
Chemical reactions of alcohols: Acidic nature (reaction with Na, K), esterification (Fischer esterification)
Lucas test for distinguishing 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols (ZnCl2 + conc HCl: 3° immediately turbid, 2° in 5 min, 1° on heating)
Dehydration of alcohols to alkenes (mechanism via carbocation, 3° > 2° > 1°), oxidation (PCC to aldehyde, Jones reagent / KMnO4 to carboxylic acid)
Phenols: Nomenclature, preparation from cumene (cumene hydroperoxide process), diazonium salts, and chlorobenzene (Dow's process)
Acidic character of phenol (resonance stabilized phenoxide ion, substituent effects: -NO2 increases acidity, picric acid)
Reactions of phenol: Electrophilic substitution (bromination with Br2/H2O gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol vs Br2/CS2 gives p-bromophenol)
Kolbe's reaction (phenol + NaOH + CO2 → Salicylic acid) and Reimer-Tiemann reaction (phenol + CHCl3 + KOH → Salicylaldehyde)
Ethers: Nomenclature, Williamson ether synthesis (R-X + R'-O⁻ Na⁺ → R-O-R', primary halide preferred to avoid elimination)
Cleavage of C-O bond by HI (R-O-R' + HI: I⁻ attacks less hindered primary/secondary alkyl group, but 3° alkyl gives 3° iodide via S_N1)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Hydroboration-oxidation gives anti-Markovnikov alcohol; Cumene process yields phenol + acetone; Williamson synthesis: alkyl halide must be 1°; Lucas test distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols

Chemistry.name: Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Nomenclature and structure of carbonyl group (polar C=O double bond, electrophilic carbon)

Preparation of aldehydes and ketones: Rosenmund reduction (R-COCl + H2/Pd-BaSO4), Stephen reaction (R-CN + SnCl2/HCl), Etard reaction (Toluene + CrO2Cl2 → Benzaldehyde), Gatterman-Koch reaction, Ozonolysis of alkenes, Hydration of alkynes
Nucleophilic addition reactions: Addition of HCN, NaHSO3, Alcohols (acetal and ketal formation), and Ammonia derivatives (2,4-DNP Brady's reagent, semicarbazide, hydroxylamine)
Reactivity order of carbonyl compounds: HCHO > RCHO > R-CO-R (steric hindrance and electronic +I factors)
Oxidation reactions: Tollens' test (silver mirror test for aldehydes) and Fehling's test (red Cu2O precipitate)
Iodoform reaction (haloform test): given by compounds containing CH3-C=O or CH3-CH(OH)- group (forms yellow CHI3 precipitate)
Reactions due to alpha-hydrogen: Aldol condensation and Cross-aldol condensation (dilute NaOH), Cannizzaro reaction (absence of alpha-H, 50% KOH: disproportionation into alcohol and carboxylate salt)
Carboxylic acids: Nomenclature, acidic nature (pKa values, electron withdrawing -I/-M groups increase acidity, fluoroacetic > chloroacetic > bromoacetic)
Reactions of carboxylic acids: Formation of anhydrides, esters, acyl chlorides, amides
Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction (alpha-halogenation using red P and X2), Decarboxylation (soda-lime NaOH + CaO)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Iodoform test identifies CH3-C=O group, Aldol requires alpha-H, Cannizzaro requires NO alpha-H (HCHO, Benzaldehyde), HVZ introduces halogen at alpha position

Chemistry.name: Amines (Organic Nitrogen Compounds)
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Classification of amines (1°, 2°, 3° and quaternary ammonium salts), IUPAC nomenclature, structure of amine group (pyramidal, sp³ with lone pair)
Methods of preparation: Reduction of nitro compounds (Fe/HCl, Sn/HCl, H2/Pd), Ammonolysis of alkyl halides (Hoffmann's ammonolysis), Reduction of nitriles and amides (LiAlH4)
Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis (exclusively for aliphatic primary amines, aryl amines cannot be prepared)
Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction (R-CONH2 + Br2 + 4KOH → R-NH2 + K2CO3 + 2KBr + 2H2O, gives 1° amine with one less carbon)
Basic character of amines: pKb values, comparison of basic strength in gaseous phase (3° > 2° > 1° > NH3) vs aqueous solution (Ethyl: 2° > 3° > 1° > NH3; Methyl: 2° > 1° > 3° > NH3)
Aromatic amines (Aniline): less basic than aliphatic amines due to resonance stabilization of aniline lone pair
Chemical reactions: Carbylamine test / isocyanide test (aliphatic & aromatic 1° amines + CHCl3 + alc KOH → foul smelling R-NC)
Reaction with nitrous acid (HNO2 / NaNO2 + HCl): 1° aliphatic amines give unstable diazonium salts decomposing to alcohols and N2 gas
Hinsberg test: Benzenesulphonyl chloride distinguishes 1° (soluble in alkali), 2° (insoluble in alkali), and 3° amines (no reaction)

Diazonium salts (Ar-N2⁺ X⁻): Diazotization reaction of aniline at 0-5 °C, Sandmeyer reaction (CuCl/HCl, CuBr/HBr, CuCN/KCN), Gatterman reaction, Coupling reactions with phenol (orange azo dye) and aniline (yellow dye)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Carbylamine test exclusively for 1° amines, Hoffmann bromamide reduces 1 carbon, Hinsberg reagent distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° amines, Diazonium coupling yields azo dyes

Chemistry.name: Biomolecules
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Carbohydrates: Classification (monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, polysaccharides), Aldoses and Ketoses
Glucose: Preparation, open-chain Fischer structure, chemical reactions proving structure (HI, NH2OH, Br2 water, HNO3, Ac2O)
Cyclic structure of glucose: Haworth projections of alpha-D-(+)-glucopyranose and beta-D-(+)-glucopyranose, Anomers (C1 stereoisomers)
Fructose: structure and Haworth projections of alpha and beta furanose forms
Disaccharides: Glycosidic linkage, Sucrose (invert sugar, non-reducing, glucose + fructose), Maltose (alpha-1,4 linkage, reducing), Lactose (beta-1,4 linkage, milk sugar)
Polysaccharides: Starch (Amylose: water soluble, unbranched, alpha-1,4 & Amylopectin: insoluble, branched, alpha-1,4 and alpha-1,6), Glycogen (animal starch), Cellulose (beta-1,4 linkage, structural)
Proteins: Amino acids (alpha-amino acids, D & L configuration, essential vs non-essential amino acids, Zwitterion, isoelectric point)
Peptide bond (-CO-NH-), classification into fibrous proteins (keratin, myosin) and globular proteins (insulin, albumin)
Structural levels: Primary (amino acid sequence), Secondary (alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheets via H-bonds), Tertiary (disulphide bonds, hydrophobic, electrostatic), Quaternary structure
Denaturation of proteins (loss of 2° and 3° structures while 1° remains intact, e.g. boiling of egg, curdling of milk)
Nucleic acids: Chemical composition (pentose sugar: ribose/deoxyribose, phosphoric acid, nitrogenous bases: A, G, C, T, U)
Nucleosides vs Nucleotides, Phosphodiester linkages, Watson-Crick double helix structure of DNA (complementary base pairing A=T, G≡C)
Vitamins: Classification into water-soluble (B-complex, C) and fat-soluble (A, D, E, K), Deficiency diseases (Scurvy, Rickets, Beri-beri, Night blindness, Pernicious anaemia)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Anomers differ at C1 carbon, Sucrose is non-reducing invert sugar, Denaturation does not break peptide bonds, Vitamin B12 and C are water soluble, DNA base pairs A=T (2 H-bonds) and G≡C (3 H-bonds)

Chemistry.name: Practical Chemistry & Qualitative Analysis
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Detection of elements in organic compounds: Lassaigne's test for Nitrogen (Prussian blue colour), Sulphur (lead acetate black ppt, sodium nitroprusside purple), and Halogens (AgNO3 test)

Identification of functional groups: unsaturation (Br2/CCl4, Baeyer's reagent), alcoholic group (ceric ammonium nitrate), phenolic group (neutral FeCl3 violet colour), aldehyde (Tollens, Fehling), carboxylic acid (NaHCO3 effervescence), amino group

Qualitative salt analysis: Systematic cation analysis (Group I: Ag+, Pb2+; Group II: Cu2+, Pb2+; Group III: Fe3+, Al3+; Group IV: Zn2+, Ni2+, Mn2+, Co2+; Group V: Ba2+, Sr2+, Ca2+; Group VI: Mg2+, NH4+)
Anion identification: Carbonate, Sulphite, Sulphide, Nitrite, Nitrate (Brown ring test FeSO4 + H2SO4), Chloride, Bromide, Iodide, Sulphate, Phosphate
Volumetric analysis / Titrations: Standard solutions, acid-base indicators, redox titrations (Oxalic acid vs KMnO4, Mohr's salt vs KMnO4)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Brown ring complex formula [Fe(H2O)5(NO)]SO4 with +1 oxidation state of Fe, Prussian blue formula Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3, Group reagent for Group III is NH4OH in presence of NH4Cl

Biology.name: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Flower structure: Whorls, pre-fertilization events, Microsporogenesis and stamen anatomy
Microsporangium: 4 wall layers (Epidermis, Endothecium, Middle layers, Tapetum - multinucleated, nutritive, secretion of sporopollenin and callase)
Pollen grain: Exine (sporopollenin - most resistant organic material, germ pores) and Intine (cellulose & pectin), 2-celled (vegetative + generative) vs 3-celled shedding
Megasporogenesis: Pistil/Carpel structure, Ovule (Integuments, Micropyle, Chalaza, Nucellus, Funiculus, Hilum)

Development of female gametophyte (Embryo sac): Monosporic development (Polygonum type: 7-celled, 8-nucleate - 3 antipodals, 2 synergids with filiform apparatus, 1 egg cell, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei)
Pollination: Autogamy, Geitonogamy (functionally cross, genetically self), Xenogamy (true cross-pollination)
Agents of pollination: Wind (anemophily - feathery stigma, non-sticky pollen), Water (hydrophily - Vallisneria, Zostera), Animals (zoophily, entomophily)
Outbreeding devices to prevent inbreeding depression: Dichogamy, Herkogamy, Self-incompatibility, Unisexuality (Dioecy)
Pollen-pistil interaction: recognition, pollen tube growth guided by synergid filiform apparatus
Double fertilization: Syngamy (Egg + Sperm → Zygote, 2n) and Triple fusion (2 polar nuclei + Sperm → Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN, 3n)

Post-fertilization developments: Endosperm development (Free-nuclear endosperm in coconut water vs cellular in kernel), Embryo development (globular, heart-shaped, mature; scutellum & coleoptile/coleorhiza in monocots)

Seed structure: Albuminous vs Exalbuminous seeds, Perisperm (persistent nucellus in black pepper & beet), Fruit development (false fruits: apple, strawberry, cashew where thalamus contributes; parthenocarpic fruits like banana)
Apomixis (asexual seed production mimicking sexual reproduction, e.g. Asteraceae and grasses) and Polyembryony (e.g. Citrus, Mango nucellar cells)
Biology.keyConcepts: Sporopollenin degrades under no known enzyme, Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms, Endosperm is triploid (3n), Coconut water is free nuclear endosperm, Apomixis preserves hybrid vigor

Biology.name: Human Reproduction
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Male reproductive system: Testes in scrotum (thermoregulation 2-2.5 °C lower), Seminiferous tubules, Sertoli cells (nutrition) and Leydig cells (androgens / testosterone)
Male accessory ducts: Rete testis, Vasa efferentia, Epididymis, Vas deferens; Accessory glands: Seminal vesicles (fructose, prostaglandins), Prostate, Bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands (lubrication)

Female reproductive system: Ovaries, Fallopian tubes (Infundibulum with fimbriae, Ampulla - site of fertilization, Isthmus), Uterus (Perimetrium, Myometrium - smooth muscle for parturition, Endometrium - cyclic changes), Vagina, External genitalia (Vulva)
Mammary glands: Alveoli, lactiferous ducts, prolactin and oxytocin hormonal control
Gametogenesis: Spermatogenesis (Spermatogonia → 1° spermatocyte → 2° spermatocyte → Spermatids → Spermatozoa via spermiogenesis and spermiation, GnRH, LH, FSH regulation)
Structure of sperm: Head (acrosome with hyaluronidase enzyme, haploid nucleus), Middle piece (spiral mitochondria / Nebenkern for motility), Tail

Oogenesis: Initiated during embryonic stage; 1° oocyte arrested in Prophase I (Diplotene); completes Meiosis I at ovulation yielding 2° oocyte and 1st polar body; arrested in Metaphase II until fertilization

Menstrual cycle: Menstrual phase (days 1-5, breakdown of endometrium due to progesterone withdrawal), Follicular / Proliferative phase (days 6-13, FSH & estrogen rise), Ovulatory surge (day 14, LH surge triggers ovulation), Luteal / Secretory phase (days 15-28, Corpus luteum secretes high progesterone)
Fertilization: Acrosomal reaction, cortical granule reaction blocking polyspermy (zona pellucida hardening), completion of Meiosis II of secondary oocyte yielding ovum and 2nd polar body
Cleavage and blastocyst formation: Morula → Blastocyst (Trophoblast outer layer + Inner Cell Mass ICM yielding embryo)
Implantation in uterine endometrium (day 7 post-fertilization), Pregnancy and Placenta formation (human chorionic gonadotropin hCG, hPL, relaxin)
Gestation (9 months), Parturition: Neuroendocrine reflex (Foetal ejection reflex, oxytocin secretion from maternal posterior pituitary), Lactation (Colostrum rich in IgA antibodies)
Biology.keyConcepts: LH surge on 14th day causes ovulation; Site of fertilization is ampulla; Trophoblast forms chorionic villi of placenta; Colostrum contains secretory IgA; Leydig cells secrete testosterone under LH

Biology.name: Reproductive Health
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Need for reproductive health, problems and strategies: Family planning (1951), RCH (Reproductive and Child Health Care) programmes
Population stabilization and birth control: Ideal contraceptive attributes
Contraceptive methods: Natural / traditional (Periodic abstinence days 10-17, Coitus interruptus, Lactational amenorrhoea up to 6 months)
Barrier methods: Condoms (prevent STDs), Diaphragms, Cervical caps, Vaults

Intrauterine Devices (IUDs): Non-medicated (Lippes loop), Copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375 - suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity), Hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20 - make uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperm)
Oral contraceptives: Combined pills (estrogen-progestogen), Saheli (Centchroman - once-a-week non-steroidal pill developed by CDRI Lucknow)
Injectables and Implants (Norplant under skin), Emergency contraception (within 72 hours of unprotected coitus)
Surgical / Permanent methods: Vasectomy (vas deferens tied/cut in males) and Tubectomy (fallopian tubes tied/cut in females)
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP): Legalized in India in 1971; safe during first trimester (up to 12 weeks); MTP Amendment Act 2017 & 2021
Amniocentesis: foetal sex determination and statutory ban to prevent female foeticide, detection of genetic disorders
Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs / STIs): Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Genital herpes, Chlamydiasis, Genital warts, Trichomoniasis, Hepatitis-B, HIV-AIDS; completely curable vs non-curable

Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART): In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) - Test Tube Baby programme, Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT - up to 8 blastomeres), Intra-Uterine Transfer (IUT - >8 blastomeres), Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT), Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), Artificial Insemination (AI) / IUI, Surrogacy
Biology.keyConcepts: Cu-releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility; LNG-20 makes cervix hostile; Saheli is non-steroidal weekly pill; ZIFT transfers embryo up to 8 blastomeres into fallopian tube, IUT >8 blastomeres into uterus

Biology.name: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Mendel's laws of inheritance: Selection of Pisum sativum (7 pairs of contrasting traits), Monohybrid cross, Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation (purity of gametes, 3:1 phenotypic, 1:2:1 genotypic)
Dihybrid cross: Law of Independent Assortment (9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio), Test cross (determines unknown dominant genotype, 1:1 or 1:1:1:1)
Deviations from Mendelian ratios: Incomplete dominance (Snapdragon / Mirabilis jalapa 1:2:1 pink flowers)
Co-dominance (ABO blood grouping in humans: IA, IB, i alleles, 6 genotypes, 4 phenotypes)
Multiple alleles (e.g. ABO blood groups, rabbit coat colour)
Pleiotropy (single gene affecting multiple phenotypic traits, e.g. Phenylketonuria, Starch synthesis in pea seeds)
Polygenic inheritance (quantitative inheritance controlled by multiple genes, e.g. Human skin colour, height, bell-shaped curve)
Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance: Sutton and Boveri (parallelism between Mendelian factors and chromosomes)
Experimental verification by Thomas Hunt Morgan using Drosophila melanogaster (fruit fly advantages: short 2-week lifecycle, sexual dimorphism, easily cultured)
Linkage and Recombination: Complete vs Incomplete linkage, Alfred Sturtevant and chromosome mapping (1% recombination = 1 centiMorgan / map unit)

Sex determination mechanisms: XX-XY (humans, Drosophila), XX-XO (grasshopper), ZZ-ZW (birds), Haplodiploidy (Honey bees: unfertilized egg develops into male drone by parthenogenesis n=16, fertilized egg into female worker/queen 2n=32)
Mutation: Gene mutations (point mutation like Sickle cell anemia, frameshift mutations) and Chromosomal aberrations (deletion, duplication, inversion, translocation)
Pedigree analysis: Symbols, autosomal dominant (Myotonic dystrophy), autosomal recessive (Sickle cell, Cystic fibrosis, PKU), X-linked recessive (Haemophilia, Colour blindness)

Mendelian disorders: Haemophilia (Queen Victoria pedigree, royal disease), Colour blindness (red-green), Sickle cell anaemia (GAG to GUG point mutation in beta-globin chain at 6th position, Glu to Val substitution), Phenylketonuria (deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase enzyme), Thalassemia (quantitative defect in globin chain synthesis: alpha vs beta thalassemia)

Chromosomal disorders (Aneuploidy due to non-disjunction of chromosomes): Down's syndrome (Trisomy 21: short stature, furrowed tongue, mental retardation, 47 chromosomes), Klinefelter's syndrome (44+XXY = 47: sterile male with gynaecomastia), Turner's syndrome (44+XO = 45: sterile female with rudimentary ovaries and webbed neck)
Biology.keyConcepts: Sickle cell: GAG to GUG codon, Glutamic acid replaced by Valine at 6th position of beta-chain; Recombination frequency = Map distance in cM; Klinefelter is 47,XXY; Turner is 45,XO; Down is trisomy 21

Biology.name: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: DNA as genetic material: Structure of polynucleotide chain, 5' phosphate, 3' OH, antiparallel strands
Watson and Crick double helix model of B-DNA: Pitch 3.4 nm, 10 base pairs per turn, distance between bp 0.34 nm
Chargaff's rules: [A] = [T] and [G] = [C], [A+G] = [T+C], (A+T)/(G+C) is species specific

Packaging of DNA helix: Nucleosome model (octamer of histones: H2A, H2B, H3, H4 in pairs, 200 bp wrapped around octamer, H1 linker histone), Euchromatin (loosely packed, transcriptionally active) vs Heterochromatin (densely packed, inactive)
Search for genetic material: Griffith's Transformation experiment (Streptococcus pneumoniae, transforming principle)
Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty experiment (DNase destroys transformation, proving DNA is genetic material)
Hershey and Chase experiment (Bacteriophage T2 with 35S labelled protein coat and 32P labelled DNA, unequivocal proof that DNA is genetic material)
DNA vs RNA: RNA as first genetic material (RNA world hypothesis), chemical stability of DNA (deoxyribose, thymine instead of uracil, double strand)
DNA replication: Semiconservative replication proof by Meselson and Stahl using 15N heavy nitrogen in E. coli, Taylor's experiment using radioactive thymidine in Vicia faba

Mechanism of DNA replication: Replication fork, Origin of replication (Ori), DNA-dependent DNA polymerase (5' to 3' synthesis only), Leading strand (continuous) and Lagging strand (discontinuous Okazaki fragments joined by DNA ligase), Primase (RNA primer)
Transcription: Transcription unit (Promoter, Structural gene, Terminator)
Transcription in Prokaryotes: Single RNA polymerase, initiation factor sigma, termination factor rho
Transcription in Eukaryotes: RNA Polymerase I (rRNA: 28S, 18S, 5.8S), RNA Polymerase II (hnRNA / precursor of mRNA), RNA Polymerase III (tRNA, 5S rRNA, snRNA)

Post-transcriptional processing of hnRNA: Splicing (introns removed by spliceosome, exons joined), Capping (7-methylguanosine triphosphate at 5' end), Tailing (Polyadenylation / 200-300 adenylate residues at 3' end)
Genetic code: Triplet codons (64 codons: 61 sense codons, 3 stop codons: UAA, UAG, UGA), properties (Universal, Degenerate, Unambiguous, Commaless), Initiator codon (AUG codes for Methionine)
tRNA: Adapter molecule, cloverleaf 2D secondary structure, inverted L-shaped 3D structure, anticodon loop and amino acid acceptor end

Translation (Protein synthesis): Aminoacylation of tRNA (charging of tRNA), Ribosome (small and large subunits, A, P, E sites), Initiation, Elongation (peptidyl transferase 23S rRNA in bacteria), Termination

Regulation of gene expression in prokaryotes: Operon concept by Jacob and Monod, Lac operon in E. coli (regulatory gene i codes for repressor, promoter p, operator o, structural genes z: beta-galactosidase, y: permease, a: transacetylase; Inducer is Allolactose/Lactose; Negative and inducible regulation)

Human Genome Project (HGP): Goals, methodologies (ESTs vs Sequence Annotation), major findings (3.1647 billion bp, average gene 3000 bp, dystrophin largest gene 2.4 million bp, chromosome 1 has most genes 2968, Y chromosome fewest 231, <2% genome codes for proteins)
DNA Fingerprinting: Developed by Alec Jeffreys, Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) / Minisatellites as probes, Southern blotting, forensic and paternity applications
Biology.keyConcepts: Meselson-Stahl 15N proves semiconservative replication; Hershey-Chase 32P proves DNA is genetic material; Lac operon: z=beta-gal, y=permease, a=transacetylase; Start codon AUG; Stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA; 23S rRNA is ribozyme

Biology.name: Evolution
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Origin of life: Big Bang theory, formation of Earth (4.5 billion years ago), primitive reducing atmosphere (CH4, NH3, H2O vapour, H2, no free oxygen)

Theories of origin of life: Abiogenesis, Biogenesis (Louis Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiment disproved spontaneous generation), Panspermia / Cosmozoic theory, Chemical evolution (Oparin and Haldane theory)
Miller-Urey experiment (1953): Electric discharge in closed flask containing CH4, NH3, H2, H2O (2:1:2 ratio) at 800 °C, produced amino acids (glycine, alanine, aspartic acid)

Evidences for biological evolution: Paleontological evidence (fossils in sedimentary rocks), Embryological evidence (Ernst Haeckel biogenetic law: ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny; disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer)
Comparative anatomy and morphology: Homologous organs (divergent evolution, common ancestry, e.g. forelimbs of cheetah, whale, bat, human; thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita)
Analogous organs (convergent evolution, different origin, similar function, e.g. wings of bird and butterfly; eye of octopus and mammal; sweet potato root and potato stem)
Adaptive radiation: Evolution of different species from common point radiating to other geographical areas (Darwin's Finches in Galapagos islands, Australian marsupials)

Biological evolution: Lamarckism (use and disuse of organs, inheritance of acquired characters), Darwinism (Natural selection, survival of the fittest, overproduction, struggle for existence, branching descent)
Industrial melanism in England (Biston betularia: peppered moth vs dark melanic moth due to pollution and lichen cover)
Mechanism of evolution: Hugo de Vries Mutation theory (mutations are random and directionless, saltation: single-step large mutation causes speciation)
Hardy-Weinberg Principle: Allelic frequencies in a population remain constant and stable from generation to generation in absence of evolutionary forces
Equation: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 (p = frequency of dominant allele, q = frequency of recessive allele, 2pq = heterozygotes)

Factors affecting Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium: Gene migration / gene flow, Genetic drift (Sewall Wright effect: Founder effect and Bottleneck effect in small populations), Mutation, Genetic recombination, Natural selection (Stabilizing, Directional, Disruptive selections)

Brief account of evolution: First cellular forms (2000 mya), Invertebrates (500 mya), Jawless fish (350 mya), Coelacanth (lobefin ancestor of amphibians, caught in South Africa 1938), Dinosaurs extinction (65 mya)

Origin and evolution of man: Dryopithecus (ape-like) & Ramapithecus (man-like, 15 mya), Australopithecus (2 mya, walked upright, brain 500 cc, hunted with stone weapons), Homo habilis (first human-like hominid, brain 650-800 cc, did not eat meat), Homo erectus (1.5 mya, Java man, brain 900 cc, ate meat, used fire), Neanderthal man (100,000-40,000 years ago, brain 1400 cc, buried their dead, used hides), Homo sapiens (modern man, arose in Africa 75,000-10,000 years ago, cave paintings 18,000 years ago)
Biology.keyConcepts: Homology = Divergent evolution = Common ancestor; Analogy = Convergent evolution; Hardy-Weinberg: p² + 2pq + q² = 1; Neanderthal brain 1400 cc; Homo habilis first tool maker

Biology.name: Human Health and Disease
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Common infectious human diseases: Causative agent, symptoms, mode of transmission, and prevention:
- Typhoid: Salmonella typhi, Widal test, Mary Mallon (Typhoid Mary)
- Pneumonia: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (alveoli filled with fluid, finger nails turn blue)
- Common cold: Rhino viruses (infects nose and respiratory tract, but NOT lungs)

- Malaria: Plasmodium vivax, P. malariae, P. falciparum (malignant tertian malaria, fatal); Life cycle in human (sporozoites invade liver cells, RBC rupture releases hemozoin toxin causing periodic chills and fever) and female Anopheles mosquito vector (sexual reproduction in gut, salivary glands store sporozoites)
- Amoebiasis (Amoebic dysentery): Entamoeba histolytica (houseflies mechanical carriers)
- Ascariasis: Ascaris lumbricoides (intestinal roundworm, internal bleeding, muscular pain)
- Elephantiasis / Filariasis: Wuchereria bancrofti and W. malayi (chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels of lower limbs, female Culex vector)
- Ringworm: Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton (fungal dry scaly lesions on skin, scalp, nails)

Immunity: Innate immunity (non-specific, 4 barriers: Physical - skin & mucus; Physiological - acid in stomach, saliva, tears with lysozyme; Cellular - PMNL neutrophils, monocytes, natural killer cells; Cytokine - interferons protect non-infected cells from virus)
Acquired immunity: Specific, pathogen memory, Primary response (slow, IgM) and Secondary / Anamnestic response (rapid, high intensity, IgG)
Humoral immune response: B-lymphocytes produce antibodies (immunoglobulins: H2L2 structure - two heavy chains, two light chains, IgA, IgD, IgE, IgG, IgM)
Cell-mediated immune response: T-lymphocytes (Helper T, Cytotoxic T, Suppressor T), responsible for graft rejection in organ transplantation (immunosuppressant Cyclosporin A)
Active immunity (natural infection or vaccination) vs Passive immunity (pre-formed antibodies: colostrum IgA, anti-tetanus serum, anti-venom)
Vaccination and Immunization: Principle of immunological memory, recombinant DNA vaccines (Hepatitis B vaccine produced from yeast)
Allergies: Exaggerated immune response to allergens (pollen, dust, mites), IgE antibodies, release of histamine and serotonin from mast cells; treated with antihistamines, adrenaline, steroids
Autoimmunity: Immune system attacks self-antigens (Rheumatoid arthritis, Myasthenia gravis, Type 1 Diabetes)

Immune system in body: Primary lymphoid organs (Bone marrow where all blood cells including lymphocytes mature, Thymus gland where T-cells mature) and Secondary lymphoid organs (Spleen - reservoir of erythrocytes, Lymph nodes, Tonsils, Peyer's patches, MALT - Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue accounts for 50% of lymphoid tissue)

AIDS (Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome): Causative agent HIV (Retrovirus with single-stranded RNA genome and reverse transcriptase enzyme), transmission modes, HIV replication cycle (Reverse transcription in macrophages 'HIV factory' → viral DNA integrates into host genome → infects and progressively destroys Helper T-lymphocytes / CD4+ cells → opportunistic infections by Mycobacterium, Toxoplasma)
Diagnosis by ELISA, confirmation by Western Blot; Prevention by NACO; Antiretroviral drugs only prolong life
Cancer: Characteristics (uncontrolled cell division, loss of contact inhibition, metastasis / invasion of distant sites via blood)
Types of tumors: Benign (confined to original location) and Malignant (cancerous, neoplastic cells)

Causes of cancer (Carcinogens): Physical (ionizing radiations: X-rays, gamma rays; non-ionizing: UV rays), Chemical (tobacco smoke causes lung cancer), Biological (Oncogenic viruses, cellular oncogenes / proto-oncogenes activated to oncogenes)

Cancer detection (biopsy, histopathology, radiography, CT scan, MRI, monoclonal antibodies), Treatment (Surgery, Radiation therapy, Chemotherapy, Immunotherapy: alpha-interferon biological response modifier)
Drugs and Alcohol Abuse: Opioids (Morphine, Heroin / smack - diacetylmorphine, binds opioid receptors in CNS and GIT, depressant slowing body functions)
Cannabinoids (Marijuana, hashish, charas, ganja - from Cannabis sativa, binds cannabinoid receptors in brain, affects cardiovascular system)
Coca alkaloids / Cocaine (Erythroxylum coca - interferes with dopamine transport, potent CNS stimulant, euphoria, hallucinations at high doses), Hallucinogens (Atropa belladonna, Datura, LSD)
Biology.keyConcepts: Malarial parasite: Sporozoite is infectious stage, Hemozoin toxin causes chill/fever; HIV attacks Helper T-cells (CD4+); MALT is 50% of lymphoid tissue; Contact inhibition lost in cancer; IgE in allergy

Biology.name: Microbes in Human Welfare
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Microbes in household products: Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB / Lactobacillus) converts milk to curd, increases nutritional quality by enriching Vitamin B12, checks disease-causing microbes in gut
Fermentation of dough for dosa, idli (CO2 production), bread making using Brewer's/Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
Traditional drink Toddy from fermented palm sap, Swiss cheese large holes due to CO2 by Propionibacterium sharmanii, Roquefort cheese ripened by specific fungi
Microbes in industrial products: Fermented beverages (wine, beer without distillation; whisky, brandy, rum with distillation)
Antibiotics: Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin from Penicillium notatum (inhibited Staphylococcus), full potential established by Ernst Chain and Howard Florey
Chemicals, enzymes, and bioactive molecules:
- Citric acid (Aspergillus niger fungus), Acetic acid (Acetobacter aceti bacterium), Butyric acid (Clostridium butylicum), Lactic acid (Lactobacillus)
- Ethanol by Saccharomyces cerevisiae
- Lipases (detergents to remove oily stains), Pectinases and Proteases (clearing bottled fruit juices)
- Streptokinase produced by Streptococcus (modified by genetic engineering, used as 'clot buster' for myocardial infarction patients)
- Cyclosporin A produced by Trichoderma polysporum fungus (immunosuppressive agent in organ transplant patients)
- Statins produced by Monascus purpureus yeast (blood-cholesterol lowering agent, competitive inhibitor of cholesterol synthesizing enzyme)
Microbes in sewage treatment: Primary treatment (physical removal of floating debris and grit by filtration and sedimentation)

Secondary treatment (biological treatment): Aerobic microbes in aeration tanks form flocs, digest organic matter, drastically reduce BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand: measure of organic pollution in water)
Sedimentation in settling tanks yields activated sludge; part returned as inoculum, major part pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters where anaerobic bacteria produce Biogas (methane CH4, H2S, CO2)
Microbes in biogas production: Methanogens (Methanobacterium) in anaerobic cattle dung (gobar gas plant components by KVIC and IARI)

Microbes as biocontrol agents: Ladybird beetle (against aphids), Dragonflies (against mosquitoes), Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt cotton bio-pesticide, Cry proteins kill lepidopteran larvae), Trichoderma fungus (root ecosystem biocontrol), Baculoviruses (genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus: species-specific narrow spectrum insecticidal applications, no harm to non-target organisms)
Microbes as biofertilizers: Rhizobium (symbiotic N2-fixing in legumes), Azotobacter and Azospirillum (free-living N2 fixers in soil)
Mycorrhiza: Fungal symbiosis with roots (genus Glomus: absorbs phosphorus for plant, resistance to root pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought)
Cyanobacteria: Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria (autotrophic N2 fixers in paddy fields, add organic matter to soil)
Biology.keyConcepts: BOD decreases as water gets purified; Clot buster = Streptokinase; Immunosuppressive = Cyclosporin A (Trichoderma polysporum); Cholesterol lowering = Statins (Monascus purpureus); Nucleopolyhedrovirus has narrow spectrum

Biology.name: Biotechnology: Principles & Processes
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Definition of biotechnology (EFB European Federation of Biotechnology: integration of natural science and organisms/cells/molecular analogues for products and services)

Two core techniques of biotechnology: Genetic engineering (creation of recombinant DNA, gene cloning, gene transfer) and Bioprocess engineering (maintenance of sterile ambience for manufacturing antibiotics, vaccines, enzymes)
First recombinant DNA constructed by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer (1972) by linking antibiotic resistance gene with plasmid vector of Salmonella typhimurium
Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology: Restriction enzymes (Molecular scissors: Endonucleases vs Exonucleases, discovery by Arber, Nathan, Smith)

Nomenclature of restriction enzymes (e.g. EcoRI: Escherichia coli RY13, first endonuclease), recognition of specific palindromic nucleotide sequences (EcoRI recognizes 5'-GAATTC-3', cuts between G and A producing sticky single-stranded overhangs)
DNA Ligase (molecular glue) and DNA polymerases

Gel Electrophoresis: Separation of DNA fragments based on size and negative charge towards anode (+); agarose gel matrix; staining with Ethidium Bromide (EtBr) under UV light produces bright orange bands; Elution (extraction from gel piece)
Cloning Vectors: Plasmids and Bacteriophages (high copy number); Essential features of vector:
- Origin of replication (Ori): controls copy number of linked DNA
- Selectable marker: identifies and selects transformants while eliminating non-transformants (antibiotic resistance genes amp^R, tet^R in pBR322 plasmid)

- Cloning sites: unique recognition sites; Insertional inactivation (inserting foreign gene into tet^R or beta-galactosidase / lacZ gene: recombinants produce white colonies, non-recombinants produce blue colonies in presence of chromogenic X-gal substrate)
- Vectors for cloning in plants (Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens disarmed) and animals (Retroviruses disarmed)

Competent host transformation methods: Divalent cation treatment (Ca2+), heat shock (42 °C), Microinjection (direct injection into animal nucleus), Gene gun / Biolistics (tungsten/gold particles coated with DNA for plant cells), Disarmed pathogens

Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology: Isolation of DNA (cell lysis by lysozyme, cellulase, chitinase; protein removal by protease; RNA removal by RNase; precipitation with chilled ethanol yielding DNA spooling)

Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR): In vitro amplification of DNA sequence developed by Kary Mullis; 3 steps: Denaturation (94 °C), Primer Annealing (54 °C), Extension (72 °C using thermostable Taq DNA polymerase isolated from bacterium Thermus aquaticus); 1 billion fold amplification in 30 cycles

Bioreactors: Large vessels (100-1000 litres) providing optimal growth conditions (temperature, pH, substrate, oxygen); Stirred-tank bioreactor (cylindrical with curved base, agitator, sparger for oxygen bubbling, foam breaker)
Downstream Processing: Separation, purification, quality control testing, and preservation of finished biotech product before marketing
Biology.keyConcepts: EcoRI cuts 5'-GAATTC-3'; DNA is negatively charged and moves towards anode (+); Ethidium bromide + UV gives bright orange bands; Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus is heat-stable up to 95 °C; Insertional inactivation of lacZ gives white recombinant colonies

Biology.name: Biotechnology and Its Applications
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Applications of biotechnology in agriculture: Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs): advantages (tolerance to abiotic stresses, pest resistance, reduced post-harvest losses, increased nutritional value like Golden Rice enriched with Vitamin A)

Bt Cotton: Soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis produces crystal endotoxin proteins (Cry proteins); inactive protoxin converted to active toxin in alkaline pH of insect gut, binds midgut epithelial cells, creates pores, cell lysis and insect death
Specific Cry genes: cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms, cryIAb controls corn borer
Pest resistant plants: RNA interference (RNAi) in tobacco against nematode Meloidogyne incognita (infects roots reducing yield)

Mechanism of RNAi: Cellular defense in all eukaryotes; cellular introduction of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) via Agrobacterium vectors triggers Dicer and RISC complex, causing sequence-specific mRNA silencing/cleavage, preventing translation of nematode parasite mRNA

Biotechnological applications in medicine: Genetically engineered insulin (Humulin by Eli Lilly in 1983: human proinsulin contains A chain, B chain, and C peptide; synthesized separate A and B chains in E. coli linked by disulphide bonds; mature insulin lacks C peptide)

Gene Therapy: First clinical gene therapy (1990) on a 4-year-old girl with Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causing Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID); functional ADA cDNA introduced into cultured patient lymphocytes using retroviral vector; permanent cure requires introducing gene into bone marrow stem cells at early embryonic stage
Molecular diagnosis: Early detection of diseases before visible symptoms; PCR (detects low copy HIV, oncogene mutations) and ELISA (antigen-antibody interactions)

Transgenic animals: Mice, rats, rabbits, pigs, cows, sheep, fish created for study of physiology and development, study of diseases (cancer, cystic fibrosis, Alzheimer's), biological products (Alpha-1-antitrypsin for emphysema, first transgenic cow Rosie produced milk with human alpha-lactalbumin 2.4 g/L), vaccine safety testing (polio vaccine in transgenic mice), chemical toxicity testing
Ethical issues: GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee) in India regulates GMO safety and environmental release

Biopiracy: Exploitation and unauthorized commercial patenting of bioresources and traditional knowledge without permission of indigenous people (patenting of Indian Basmati rice by Texas company RiceTec in 1997, turmeric, neem)
Biology.keyConcepts: Humulin lacks C-peptide; First gene therapy for ADA deficiency; RNAi uses dsRNA to silence nematode mRNA; Rosie cow produced human alpha-lactalbumin; CryIAc & CryIIAb control cotton bollworms, CryIAb controls corn borer

Biology.name: Organisms and Populations
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Organism and its environment: Major abiotic factors - Temperature (stenothermal vs eurythermal), Water (stenohaline vs euryhaline), Light (photoperiodism), Soil

Responses to abiotic factors: Regulators (maintain homeostatic internal body temperature, e.g. all birds and mammals), Conformers (99% animals and nearly all plants, osmotic and body temp changes with environment), Migrate (Keoladeo National Park in Bharatpur hosts Siberian cranes), Suspend (hibernation in bears, aestivation in snails, diapause in zooplankton)

Adaptations: Kangaroo rat (internal fat oxidation producing water, concentrated urine), Desert plants (thick cuticle, sunken stomata, CAM pathway, leaves modified to spines like Opuntia), Allen's rule (mammals in colder climates have shorter ears and limbs to minimize heat loss), Blubber thick fat in seals, High-altitude adaptation (increased RBC count, increased breathing rate, decreased binding affinity of haemoglobin)
Populations: Population attributes - Birth rate (natality), Death rate (mortality), Sex ratio, Age pyramids (Expanding / triangular, Stable / bell-shaped, Declining / urn-shaped)

Population growth models: Exponential growth (unlimited resources, J-shaped curve, dN/dt = rN, N_t = N_0 e^rt, r = intrinsic rate of natural increase) and Logistic growth (Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth, limited resources, sigmoid S-shaped curve, dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K), K = Carrying capacity)

Population interactions: Predation (+/-: sparrow eating seeds, tigers eating deer, herbivore control, Prickly pear cactus controlled by Cactoblastis moth, monarch butterfly poisonous distasteful predator defense)

Competition (-/-: Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle: two closely related species competing for same limiting resource cannot coexist indefinitely, e.g. Abingdon tortoise in Galapagos became extinct after goats introduced; Resource partitioning by MacArthur: 5 species of warblers coexisting by foraging differences)
Parasitism (+/-: Ectoparasites like lice, ticks, Cuscuta; Endoparasites; Brood parasitism: Cuckoo / Koel lays eggs in Crow's nest)
Commensalism (+/0: Orchid growing as epiphyte on mango branch, Barnacles on whale back, Sea anemone and clownfish, Cattle egret and grazing cattle)

Mutualism (+/+: Lichen mutualism between algae and fungi, Mycorrhiza between fungi and higher plant roots, Fig tree and pollinator wasp, Ophrys orchid sexual deceit mimicking female Colpa wasp for pseudocopulation)
Biology.keyConcepts: dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K); Gause's Competitive Exclusion; Allen's rule: shorter extremities in cold climates; MacArthur's resource partitioning; Ophrys sexual deceit; Brood parasitism in Koel and Crow

Biology.name: Ecosystem
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Ecosystem: Structure and function, components - Productivity, Decomposition, Energy flow, and Nutrient cycling

Productivity: Primary production, Gross Primary Productivity (GPP: total rate of organic matter synthesis) and Net Primary Productivity (NPP = GPP - R, where R is respiration loss), Secondary productivity by consumers

Decomposition: Breakdown of complex organic matter (detritus) into inorganic substances; 5 steps: Fragmentation (earthworms detritivores), Leaching (water-soluble inorganic nutrients seep into soil horizon), Catabolism (fungal and bacterial enzymes degrade detritus), Humification (leads to dark amorphous colloidal humus, reservoir of nutrients, resistant to microbial action), Mineralization

Factors affecting decomposition: Oxygen availability (aerobic favored), chemical composition (slow if rich in lignin and chitin, fast if rich in nitrogen and water-soluble sugars), temperature and moisture
Energy flow: Unidirectional flow of energy from sun (PAR Photosynthetically Active Radiation: only 50% of incident radiation; plants capture only 2-10% of PAR)
Food chains: Grazing Food Chain (GFC: Grass → Deer → Lion) and Detritus Food Chain (DFC: Dead matter → Fungi/Bacteria)
Lindeman's 10% law of energy transfer across trophic levels
Ecological pyramids (Charles Elton): Pyramid of numbers (upright in grassland, inverted in tree ecosystem with parasites)
Pyramid of biomass (upright in terrestrial grasslands/forests; INVERTED in aquatic ocean/pond ecosystem: small standing crop of phytoplankton supports large zooplankton/fishes)
Pyramid of energy: ALWAYS upright, can never be inverted because energy is lost as heat at each step (second law of thermodynamics)
Biology.keyConcepts: NPP = GPP - R; 10% law of energy; Pyramid of energy is ALWAYS upright; Aquatic biomass pyramid is inverted (phytoplankton < zooplankton < fish); PAR is 50% of solar radiation

Biology.name: Biodiversity and Its Conservation
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Concept of biodiversity (Edward Wilson): Genetic diversity (Rauwolfia vomitoria producing reserpine, 50,000 strains of rice, 1,000 mango varieties), Species diversity (Western Ghats have greater amphibian diversity than Eastern Ghats), Ecological diversity (India has deserts, rain forests, mangroves, coral reefs, wetlands)
Global biodiversity estimates: Robert May's global estimate of 7 million species (only 1.5 million currently named; 70% animals of which 70% insects, 22% plants)
India as Mega-diversity nation: India has only 2.4% of world's land area but shares 8.1% of global species diversity (one of 12 mega-diversity nations)

Patterns of biodiversity: Latitudinal gradients (species diversity decreases from equator to poles; Tropics harbour more species due to historical evolutionary time undisturbed by glaciations, constant predictable environment, greater solar energy input; Amazon rainforest in South America is 'lungs of the planet', harbours greatest biodiversity)

Species-Area relationship: Alexander von Humboldt (log S = log C + Z log A, where S = species richness, A = area, Z = slope of line regression coefficient usually 0.1 to 0.2; 0.6 to 1.2 for entire continents)
Importance of species diversity to ecosystem: David Tilman's long-term field plots (plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass)
Paul Ehrlich's Rivet Popper hypothesis (aeroplane = ecosystem, rivets = species; loss of rivets in wings / keystone species threatens flight safety / ecosystem stability)

Loss of Biodiversity: IUCN Red List (2004) documents extinction of 784 species in 500 years (Dodo in Mauritius, Quagga in Africa, Thylacine in Australia, Steller's Sea Cow in Russia, three subspecies of tiger: Bali, Javan, Caspian)
Causes of biodiversity loss - 'The Evil Quartet':
1. Habitat loss and fragmentation (most important cause: tropical rainforests reduced from 14% to 6% of earth's land surface; Amazon forest being cut for soybean cultivation)
2. Over-exploitation (Steller's sea cow, passenger pigeon extinct due to human greed)

3. Alien species invasions (Nile perch introduced in Lake Victoria led to extinction of 200+ cichlid fish species; invasive weeds: Parthenium / carrot grass, Lantana, Water hyacinth / Eichhornia 'Terror of Bengal'; African catfish Clarias gariepinus threatens indigenous catfishes)
4. Co-extinctions (obligate mutualism: extinction of host fish leads to extinction of unique parasites)

Biodiversity conservation: Narrowly utilitarian (food, firewood, medicines), Broadly utilitarian (Amazon produces 20% of oxygen, pollination, aesthetic pleasures), Ethical arguments (moral duty to protect all co-inhabitants)

Conservation strategies: In situ conservation (On-site protection in natural habitat: 34 Global Biodiversity Hotspots like Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Himalaya; 14 Biosphere Reserves, 106+ National Parks, 500+ Wildlife Sanctuaries, Sacred Groves like Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, Aravalli Hills in Rajasthan)

Ex situ conservation (Off-site protection outside natural habitat: Zoological parks, Botanical gardens, Wildlife safari parks, Cryopreservation of gametes at -196 °C in liquid nitrogen, Seed banks, Tissue culture micropropagation)

International conventions: Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro (1992) for conservation of biodiversity, World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg, South Africa (2002: 190 countries pledged significant reduction in biodiversity loss rate)
Biology.keyConcepts: Alexander von Humboldt Species-Area: log S = log C + Z log A; Evil Quartet: Habitat loss is #1; In situ = National Parks, Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Sacred Groves; Ex situ = Cryopreservation, Seed Banks, Botanical Gardens, Zoos
